title: A tube on a tube

objective.text: Describe the embryo's body plan once folding is done at the end of week 4.

body.general: What shape is the embryo once it has folded? It is a tube on a tube: the neural tube (future brain and spinal cord) along the back, the gut tube below [f1]. Both form at almost the same time, in weeks 3–4 [f1]. The side walls of the body swing down and meet in the midline, closing the belly side [f2]. Head and tail folds help by curling the embryo [f3]. One gap stays open: the stalk that becomes the umbilical cord [f4]. There a narrow duct still joins the gut to the yolk sac [f4].
body.mbbs: In weeks 3–4 the ectoderm rolls into the neural tube dorsally while the endoderm rolls into the gut tube ventrally, at almost the same time [f1]. The result is a tube on a tube, held together by mesoderm [f1]. The lateral body-wall folds, made of parietal mesoderm, ectoderm and cells from nearby somites, swing ventrally and meet in the midline [f2]. This closes the ventral body wall by the end of week 4 [f2]. Head and tail folds help by curling the embryo [f3]. Closure stays open only at the connecting stalk, the future umbilical cord [f4]. There the gut still opens into the yolk sac through the vitelline duct [f4]. The duct later thins and disappears with the yolk sac in months 2–3 [f5]. Where the gut meets the dorsal body wall, the parietal and visceral mesoderm layers stay continuous [f6].

facts.text: In weeks 3–4 the ectoderm rolls up into the neural tube on the back. Almost at the same time the endoderm rolls into the gut tube below, with mesoderm between.
facts.note: R06 CS10–12 confirms each process; the 'tube on a tube' picture is the book's

facts.text: The lateral body-wall folds swing ventrally and meet in the midline, closing the ventral body wall by the end of week 4. They are parietal mesoderm, ectoderm and cells from nearby somites.
facts.note: later muscle and rib layer: D-043 (a), see f7

facts.text: Head and tail folds help close the body by curling the embryo.
Closure stays open at one place, the connecting stalk (future umbilical cord), where the gut still opens into the yolk sac through the vitelline duct.
facts.note: R06 CS12–13: umbilical stalk forms; amnion closes around it

facts.text: The vitelline duct joins the cord, thins and disappears with the yolk sac in months 2–3.
Where the gut meets the dorsal body wall, the parietal and visceral mesoderm layers stay continuous with each other.
Beyond Langman (human 3D study): the later muscle, rib and sternum layer of the front wall spreads toward the midline from stage 15 to 23. This happens mostly through faster growth of the back.
facts.note: D-043 (a) recommended option (2); studied the later musculoskeletal wall, not the week-4 somatopleure

misconceptions.wrong: The gut tube and the neural tube form one after the other.
misconceptions.right: They form at almost the same time, in weeks 3–4.

checks.prompt: When do the neural tube and the gut tube form?
options: The gut tube first, the neural tube weeks later
The neural tube first, the gut tube after week 8
At almost the same time, in weeks 3–4
Only after the ventral body wall has closed
checks.why: While the ectoderm rolls into the neural tube, the endoderm rolls into the gut tube, both in weeks 3–4.

checks.prompt: At the end of week 4, where is the ventral body wall still open?
options: At the connecting stalk, the future umbilical cord
checks.why: The lateral folds meet everywhere except at the connecting stalk, where the vitelline duct still joins gut to yolk sac.

checks.prompt: In a cross-section after folding, which tube lies toward the back (dorsal)?
checks.why: The neural tube lies dorsally and the gut tube ventrally: a tube on a tube.

adult: The connecting stalk becomes the umbilical cord, and the vitelline duct normally disappears in months 2–3 [f4,f5].

remember.q: What is the body plan after folding?
remember.a: A tube on a tube: neural tube on the back, gut tube below, joined by mesoderm [f1].

remember.q: What closes the ventral body wall by the end of week 4?
remember.a: The lateral body-wall folds meeting in the midline, helped by the head and tail folds [f2,f3].

remember.q: Where does the ventral body wall stay open?
remember.a: At the connecting stalk, where the vitelline duct joins gut to yolk sac [f4].
